To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a new family of DQB alleles has been identified; (2) this family is defined by a Pro-Pro couplet in codons 55 and 56; and (3) this family is characterized by a paucity, rather than an abundance, of nucleotide variations.
1) a novel cDNA-cloning strategy was developed to facilitate DNA sequencing and 2) the nucleotide sequences of three allelic variants of the DQW3 family of DQ genes were determined and compared.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of DQB genes which are allelic variants of the DQ alpha chain.
a novel strategy for cloning and sequencing allelically variant genes, and with the characterization of DQw3 alleles, which are implicated in specific HIA-disease associations.
the molecular basis of HLA class I and II disease associations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DQw7 and w8 specificities are the result of a single amino acid difference, whereas the w9 specificity is the result of a double amino acid difference.
the DQw7, 8, and 9 specificities are defined by a single DQB gene each, DQB3, DQB4, and DQB5, respectively.
there are no nucleotide substitutions within the DQ beta chain that are unique to the DQw7, 8, and 9 specificities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DQw1 and DQw3 families of DQ genes are characterized by a high degree of sequence homology and a paucity or absence of nucleotide polymorphism.
the DQw7, DQw8, and DQw9 specificities are encoded by three allelic DQB genes, and that these genes are highly conserved among ethnic populations.
the DQw1 and DQw3 families of genes are highly conserved in their nucleotide sequences and may be the most homologous of the HLA class II gene families.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DQw7, 8, and 9 specificities are encoded by the DQB3.3, 3.1, and 3,2 genes respectively, and that the DQB3 alleles are characterized by an unusual Pro-Pro couple at codons 56 and 57.
a single-stranded cloning vector/primer strategy is a rapid and efficient method for sequencing of allelic variants of genes with a high degree of allelic variation.
the DQw1, w2, and w3 gene families represent the major DQB gene clusters and have been maintained by evolutionary forces.
